control: wrong formula (Henderson-Hasselbalch ratio inverted: [HA]/[A-] instead of [A-]/[HA]); CED 8.9.A.1 p.157: "EQN: pH = pKa + log [A−]/[HA]"
title: Henderson-Hasselbalch equation

control: explicitly excluded by the CED; 8.9 Exclusion Statement p.157: "Computation of the change in pH resulting from the addition of an acid or a base to a buffer will not be assessed on the AP Exam."
title: New buffer pH after adding strong acid

control: wrong owner topic (acid-base indicators are 8.7, not 8.2); CED 8.7.A.2 p.155: "Acid-base indicators are substances that exhibit different properties (such as color) in their protonated versus deprotonated state"
title: Acid-base indicator
body: A substance that exhibits different properties (such as color) in its protonated versus deprotonated state, so that property responds to the pH of the solution.

control: hook expansion inverted (says the deprotonated form dominates below pKa); CED 8.7.A.1 p.155: "When solution pH < acid pKa, the acid form has a higher concentration than the base form."
title: Predominant form of a weak acid from pH and pKa
body: When solution pH < pKa, the acid form (HA) has a higher concentration than the base form (A−); when pH > pKa, the base form (A−) has a higher concentration than the acid form.

hooks.hook_text: Below pKa, the proton walks away

expands_to.means: the deprotonated base form A− has the higher concentration

hooks.when_to_use: when deciding whether HA or A− predominates at a given pH
hooks.caution: In an answer, state the comparison of pH to pKa and which form has the higher concentration.

control: wrong list member (HF substituted for HI in the CED's strong-acid list); CED 8.2.A.1 p.147: "Molecules of a strong acid (e.g., HCl, HBr, HI, HClO4, H2SO4, and HNO3) will completely ionize"
title: Strong acids named in the CED
body: Acids whose molecules completely ionize in aqueous solution to produce hydronium ions and the conjugate base.

control: content from another unit (standard free energy from cell potential is Unit 9, topic 9.9); no Faraday constant, cell potential, or nFE relationship appears on CED pp.148-167 (verified by text search)
title: Free energy from cell potential
